headlines.title: China’s factory-gate prices growth slows to 3.5% in July amid lower fuel prices
headlines.summary:
China’s factory-gate prices growth slowed in July, as lower domestic fuel prices eased cost pressures triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran, while high temperatures dragged manufacturing.
The producer price index (PPI) rose by 3.5 per cent year on year last month, compared with 4.1 per cent in June, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Sunday.

headlines.title_en: China's Ministry of Finance: Will issue 6 billion yuan in government bonds in Macau on August 20
headlines.summary_en: The Ministry of Finance will issue 6 billion yuan in treasury bonds in Macau on August 20. The maturity structure of this bond issuance is more diversified, which will help improve the regular issuance mechanism, provide investors with more safe and stable yuan investment options, and play a positive role in optimizing Macau's bond market ecosystem and promoting interconnection between Macau and mainland and international markets.

headlines.title_en: Guangda Futures: Non-farm payrolls hit a new low for the year, gold's bottom range is more solid
headlines.summary_en: Since the second half of the year, gold price trends have shown signs of decoupling from U.S.-Iran geopolitical tensions, with market focus mainly on whether the Fed 'dares' to raise rates. Earlier, U.S. economic data showed resilience, but inflation data was somewhat sticky, and rate hike expectations once dominated, especially as the probability of a September FOMC rate hike kept rising. However, with weakness in high-level U.S. stocks and instability in employment data, the market questioned the Fed's, especially Warsh's, 'hawkish' stance. The unexpected weakening of nonfarm payrolls directly punctured previous market pricing for a September hike, with U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar weakening simultaneously, reinforcing the view that the U.S. is struggling between high debt and stubborn inflation. headlines.title_en: Midday market review on August 10: ChiNext Index falls over 2% in half-day trading, pharma and consumer stocks rise against the trend
headlines.summary_en: 1. The market diverged noticeably in the morning, with the Shanghai Composite in positive territory and ChiNext down over 2%. Pharmas continued gains, with Baihua Pharma hitting its 5th straight limit-up; Asia-Pacific Pharma, Harsun Pharma, and Hisun Pharma among others hit limit-up. Food and other consumer stocks bucked the trend, with Huangshi Group, Xiangpiaopiao, and Yiming Food hitting limit-up. The defense sector saw a sudden rally, with Hunan Tianyan and Changcheng Military Industry hitting limit-up. On the downside, PCB, CPO and other computing hardware stocks fell, with Accelink near limit-down, and Changyingtong and Taijin New Energy down over 10%. Advancers outnumbered decliners, with over 3,400 stocks rising across Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing markets; morning turnover was 1.75 trillion yuan. At midday close, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.2%, Shenzhen Component fell 1.13%, and ChiNext fell 2.18%. 2. In terms of sectors, defense, pharma, consumer, and pork led gains; CPO, glass substrate, PCB, and 6G led losses; 3. Across the two markets, 3,253 stocks rose.
